gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the 'up to 65 °C' chamber rating hides a 1.85× spread in heater power per litre of build volume across QIDI's current enclosed printers. The figures, from QIDI's spec sheets, are Plus5 550 W ≈ 17.9 W/L, Q2 280 W ≈ 15.0 W/L and Max4 500 W ≈ 9.7 W/L. Creality's K2 Plus heater only switches on when the chamber is set above 40 °C. Bambu publishes no chamber-heater wattage for the H2D or H2S.
standout_why: us.qidi3d.com Plus 4 TechSpecs (cited) gives only 450 W + 400 W for the discontinued Plus4. desktop3dprinters.us chamber-temperature-specs (cited) lists max chamber temperature only and says outright that it has no wattage or warm-up times. 3dcalculators.com (cited) has the 400 W Plus4 heater, the 280 W Q2 heater and Plus4 owner warm-up times. It has no Plus5 or Max4 heater wattage, does not scale heater power to chamber size, and has nothing on the K2 Plus 40 °C threshold. I could not open yakja.co (cited) because of an SSL certificate error. ChatGPT's '~20 min X2D / ~25 min H2S' times have no maker source. The BambuHub H2S page, which cites Bambu's spec page, gives no heat-up time at all.
decides: ChatGPT's top pick, the Plus4, is listed as discontinued (desktop3dprinters.us). After normalising, the QIDI Plus5 ($699 at QIDI US) has the most stated chamber-heater power per litre among current models. It also has the only maker-stated steady-state figure (500 W for ABS at 25 °C ambient) and a bed QIDI says runs at full power for 3–5 minutes during warm-up. That makes it the best-supported current answer for chamber heat-up. The Max4 has the same 65 °C label but about half the heater power per litre, so 'same max temperature' should not be read as 'same warm-up'. The K2 Plus's 60 °C rating comes with a heater that only runs for setpoints above 40 °C. None of this is a measured head-to-head time; it ranks stated heater power only.
